Resampling count models, including models with several outcomes

Source: R/resample_counts.R
fit_resamples_counts.Rd

Fits a workflow or model specification to the analysis set of each resample and evaluates it on the assessment set, for every outcome. tune's fit_resamples() computes metrics for one outcome only, so models with several (countreg_mv, countreg_alloc) need this function. It also computes the out-of-sample log score of the count distribution, which compares distributions better than errors of the mean, for any engine.

Usage

fit_resamples_counts(
  object,
  resamples,
  formula = NULL,
  metrics = NULL,
  log_score = FALSE,
  summarize = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

a workflows workflow or a count_reg specification.

resamples

an rsample resampling set, such as rsample::group_vfold_cv().

formula

the model formula, for a model specification.

metrics

a yardstick metric set of numeric metrics (default RMSE and MAE).

log_score

logical; also compute the mean log probability of the held-out counts ("log_score", larger is better). For models with several outcomes it is the score of each outcome's marginal distribution.

summarize

logical; average over the resamples (TRUE) or return the values of each?

Value

A tibble with columns outcome, .metric, mean, n (resamples with a value) and std_err, or with summarize = FALSE id, outcome, .metric and .estimate.

Details

Rows without a prediction (such as new groups of a fixed-effects model) are left out of the metrics. The options marginal, re.form, allow.new.levels and newgroup of the engine argument predict_args also apply to the log score.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("parsnip", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("rsample", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("yardstick", quietly = TRUE)) {
  spec <- count_reg(family = "NB2") |>
    parsnip::set_engine("flexCountReg", method = "BFGS")
  set.seed(1)
  folds <- rsample::group_vfold_cv(washington_roads, group = ID, v = 3)
  fit_resamples_counts(spec, folds, Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength,
                       log_score = TRUE)
}
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   outcome       .metric     mean     n std_err
#>   <chr>         <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 Total_crashes rmse       0.823     3  0.0581
#> 2 Total_crashes mae        0.489     3  0.0171
#> 3 Total_crashes log_score -0.742     3  0.0143
# }
